# The golden fixture — and what was redacted from it

`real_alert.eml` is the **real captured alert email** that closed the Decision-7
validation gate on **2026-07-16**. It is not a reconstruction, and it is not
regenerated by `tests/fixtures/_generate_fixtures.py` (see the note at
`_generate_fixtures.py:93`).

The copy in this repository is **redacted for public release**. The unredacted
original was a genuine Gmail message and carried personal data that must not be
published: real mailbox addresses, the deployment's originating IP address and
ISP hostname in the `Received:` chain, DKIM/ARC signatures, Google internal
message-state tokens, and two full-resolution photographs of a private garden.

## What Decision 7 claims, and what still supports it

The claim is that the **nominal** alert format was validated
field-for-field against a real captured alert email on **2026-07-16**. That
validation was performed against the **unredacted original**, which is retained
privately and is not part of this repository.

The redaction was chosen so the claim stays honest rather than being quietly
weakened. **Every field the parser reads is carried through from the real
message unchanged** — subject, body block, attachment filenames, MIME structure
and part ordering are byte-for-byte as they arrived. The tests in
`tests/test_email_parser.py` therefore still assert against real captured values
(`GardenCatBird`, `ColumbaPalumbus`, `0.85`, `ImageId 2808`,
`2026-07-16 12:15:34`), not invented ones.

What is **not** independently reproducible from this repository alone is the
transport layer — that a real relay produced these headers in this order. That
is not something the parser reads, and no test asserts it.

## Exactly what changed

| Element | Original | Public copy |
|---|---|---|
| `Message-ID` | Gmail-issued | `<alert-20260716121536-0001@example.com>` |
| `From` / `To` / `Delivered-To` | real mailboxes | `example.com` placeholders; `Delivered-To` dropped |
| `Received` (×3), `Received-SPF`, `Return-Path` (×2) | real relay chain, originating IP, ISP hostname | **removed** |
| `ARC-Seal`, `ARC-Message-Signature`, `ARC-Authentication-Results`, `Authentication-Results` | real | **removed** |
| `DKIM-Signature`, `X-Google-DKIM-Signature` | real | **removed** |
| `X-Gm-Message-State`, `X-Gm-Gg`, `X-Received` (×2) | real | **removed** |
| Two `image/jpeg` attachments | 232 KB + 94 KB real garden frames | small synthetic JPEGs (~1 KB each) |
| `Subject` | — | **unchanged**, including its RFC 2047 encoded-word em dash |
| `Date`, `MIME-Version`, `Content-Type` + boundary | — | **unchanged** |
| `text/plain` body block | — | **unchanged, byte-for-byte** |
| Attachment filenames | — | **unchanged**, including the boxed part's RFC 2231 `filename*0*`/`filename*1*` continuation encoding |

## Why the awkward-looking details were kept

Two properties of this message are parser edge cases under test, and a naive
re-serialisation through `email.generator` would normalise both away. They were
preserved by editing the raw bytes rather than rebuilding the message:

- the **boxed** attachment declares its filename with RFC 2231 continuation
  parameters (`filename*0*` / `filename*1*`) while the **original** attachment
  uses a plain quoted string — so the fixture exercises both spellings;
- the `Subject` carries its em dash as an RFC 2047 encoded-word.

The synthetic attachments keep the real Reolink filenames, because
`src/ttr/sources/capture_time.py` decodes the capture time out of the filename
block — swapping the bytes must not disturb what the filename says. The boxed
image has a drawn rectangle so the two attachments differ and the placeholder is
obvious when opened.

## Edge-case fixtures are unaffected

The sibling fixtures in `tests/fixtures/emails/` (`both_attachments.eml`,
`missing_boxed.eml`, `zero_attachments.eml`, `malformed_body.eml`,
`test_email_ignore.eml`) are synthetic reconstructions and always were. Per
Decision 7 they remain **validated against the reconstruction only** until a real
message surfaces for each variant — which is exactly what every generated report
states.
